newsitem.title: CANADA: Kinross Gold says rock bursts at Macassa.
newsitem.headline: Kinross Gold says rock bursts at Macassa.

text.p: Kinross Gold Corp said on Monday that underground production shifts at its Macassa Mine in Kirkland Lake, Ontario were cancelled until further notice after a series of rock bursts early on Saturday.
Kinross said in a statement the rock bursts occurred in the number three shaft area after a routine longhole production blast. There were no injuries.
For the next two weeks, stockpiled Macassa ore and custom mill feed from two nearby mines would keep the mill running at full capacity, the company said.

"It is not yet possible to determine how long Macassa mine production will be interrupted and hence to determine the ultimate impact on the previously budgeted 1997 production level of 91,000 ounces of gold at a cash operating cost of approximately US$250 per ounce," Kinross said.
Kinross said it would release additional information when it was available.

It said a preliminary assessment of the damage to the shaft indicated that it was not usable between the 5,700 and 6,000 foot levels. During the assessment period, some mine workers would be laid off, Kinross said.
